decisions.reason: After two years this recruitment service remains peripheral to the firm's stated maritime strategy and shows little visible traction, so a real-options logic would favor abandoning this weak, non-core option and reallocating attention to stronger maritime and digital offerings.

This service is still a relatively low-cost option that fits the firm's crewing capabilities and maritime customer base, so management would likely keep it on the market while demand in the niche becomes clearer.
The maritime education programme builds directly on the firm's training network and early partner growth suggests enough momentum to keep investing lightly rather than exit.

Emissions monitoring and compliance services are closely aligned with regulation-driven customer demand and the firm's successful delivery before the deadline is strong evidence of value, making withdrawal unlikely.

The emissions compliance dashboard supports the firm's digitalisation path, is integrated into existing ship-management software, and likely has low incremental carrying cost, so it is worth keeping as a strategic option.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool is complementary to the firm's regulatory service bundle and integrated software platform, so management would likely retain it while customers' needs under new rules continue to develop.
